statement: What value of $x$ satisfies the equation $\sqrt{3x + 1} = 2\sqrt{x - 1}$?

choices.misconception: I squared both sides but did not square the $2$, so I solved $3x + 1 = 2(x - 1)$.
I squared the right side as $4x - 1$, multiplying only the $x$ by $4$, so I solved $3x + 1 = 4x - 1$.
I dropped both square roots and the $2$, so I solved $3x + 1 = x - 1$.

hints: Square both sides to remove the square roots.
$3x + 1 = 4x - 4$. Solve, then check your answer in the original equation.

solutions.reliable: Squaring both sides gives $3x + 1 = 4(x - 1) = 4x - 4$, so $x = 5$. Check: $\sqrt{3(5) + 1} = \sqrt{16} = 4$ and $2\sqrt{5 - 1} = 2 \cdot 2 = 4$, so $x = 5$ works.
solutions.elegant: Write $2\sqrt{x - 1} = \sqrt{4(x - 1)}$. Two square roots of nonnegative numbers are equal exactly when the numbers are equal, so $3x + 1 = 4x - 4$ and $x = 5$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
